av_event.line_text: Oh, erm, I think it's like ninety? Something like that. I don't really look, to be honest. The supervisor looks. I'm chatting with the girls, that's the best bit.
av_event.what: A man in a dark jacket walks past the open doorway to the hallway on the left behind her, taking the coat off the hook. Sana glances briefly over her shoulder towards him, then turns back to the camera still talking.

text:
A: Hiya! Can you hear me okay?
B: Yes. Martijn. Walthamstow.
A: I'm Sana, from Bolton. Erm, nice to meet you. Your room looks very, like, professional. Is that a hard hat?
B: Yes. I'm a structural engineer. I don't wear it at home.
A: [laughs] No, I didn't think... sorry. So you build buildings?
B: I design the structure. The parts that hold it up, beams, foundations. Someone else builds it.
A: Acha, okay. That sounds hard. I was rubbish at maths at college. I do packing in a warehouse, online fashion. Part-time.
B: What does packing involve, exactly?
A: Erm, you get the order on the scanner, you go and pick the item, like a dress or whatever, you put it in the bag, label, and it goes on the belt. They count how many you do an hour. Pick rate. Mine is not... it's okay. [laughs]
B: What's the target?
A: Sorry, what?
B: The rate. How many an hour are you supposed to do?
A: Oh, erm, I think it's like ninety? Something like that. I don't really look, to be honest. The supervisor looks. I'm chatting with the girls, that's the best bit.
B: Ninety an hour is fast.
A: It is! That's what I say! [laughs] Did you do that puzzle at the start?
B: Yes. One question was wrong. It had two answers.
A: Oh, thank God, I thought it was only me who was confused. So, is that your daughter, in the photo, on the beach?
B: Yes. She's fourteen. That's Zeeland, in the Netherlands. We go every summer, same place.
A: Aww, she's so pretty. Same place every year? You don't want to try somewhere new? I want to go Maldives, or Turkey, for the photos, you know, the water villas.
B: No. She likes it, I know where everything is, and we take the train. I don't like flying.
A: Oh, I love flying! Well, not the flying, the airport, the duty free. We went Dubai once, me and my husband and his sister. The malls, oh my God, so big you need a car inside. [laughs]
B: I've heard. Too big for me.
A: Does your daughter like makeup and that? Because fourteen, all the girls are on TikTok doing the routines.
B: Er, yes. More than before. I don't really know what she's watching. She doesn't tell me much now.
A: That's normal, honestly. My little sister was like that, she wouldn't talk to my mum for like a whole year. Now they're best friends. You should ask her to show you her makeup stuff, girls love that, explaining everything. My sister made me watch a forty-minute video about skincare once.
B: Forty minutes.
A: Yeah! But it made her happy, you know.
B: That's a sensible idea, actually. I'll try it.
A: Really? [laughs] Okay! Tell her a girl from Bolton said.
B: Do you have children?
A: No, not yet. Erm... not yet. Everyone asks. My mother-in-law asks every day nearly. [laughs]
B: Sorry. I didn't mean to pry.
A: No, no, it's fine! It's a normal question.
